subject: Request: temporary SLA waiver for model-5c performance regression
messages:
From: Danielle Harper <d.harper@acme.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected latency spike on model-5c (v5.1.2) — urgent update needed

Hi Laura / Monica,

We're seeing a significant p95 latency jump on model-5c (version 5.1.2) across our east-us fleet starting ~2026-08-14 06:50 UTC. Baseline p95 is ~180ms; right now we're at ~620ms for inference requests that previously were steady. Error rates are slightly elevated (~0.2%), but the primary customer impact is latency.

Attached is a snapshot from our observability export (slo-snapshot-20260814.csv). Can you confirm if this is a known degradation (new rollout, infra change, kernel update) or if this originates from model-side changes? We need an ETA for mitigation. We're on an enterprise SLA and this is impacting an active demo this afternoon.

Thanks,
Danielle Harper
Director of AI Integrations
Acme Robotics

Attachment: slo-snapshot-20260814.csv
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc:
Date: 2026-08-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spike on model-5c (v5.1.2) — request temporary SLA waiver and mitigation plan

Team,

Summary: Customer (Acme Robotics) reports p95 jumps to ~620ms starting ~06:50 UTC. Affects model-5c v5.1.2 in east-us-2 pool only. They have a time-sensitive demo at 21:00 UTC.

Ask: I need approval to request a temporary SLA waiver (48 hours) for this account tied to model-5c (v5.1.2) while we execute a staged mitigation (canary revert + kernel parameter tuning). The customer is asking for a clear rollback/mitigation plan and an agreed monitoring window.

Proposed immediate actions (high level):
- Authorize 2-hour canary revert to v5.1.0 on a 20% traffic slice in east-us-2 (targeted pool only).
- If p95 <= 250ms within 30 minutes after canary, ramp to 100% over 45 minutes.
- If p95 does not improve or error rate spikes >0.5%, abort canary and escalate to full revert + fallback to quantized model variant (5c-q8) as a safety net.
- Parallel: kernel/compilation rollback window (we'll validate if a kernel knob changed in the last deploy).

Documentation/attachments: perf-report-model-5c-aug14.pdf (initial triage), proposed-mitigation-checklist.docx.

If you approve, I'll notify the customer that Redwood requests a short SLA exception for their account tied to this model/version and share the proposed schedule. Please reply-all with 'approve' or 'do not approve' and any edits to the plan.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: perf-report-model-5c-aug14.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spike on model-5c (v5.1.2) — technical plan and rollback triggers

Laura / Rishi,

I've pulled the runtime traces for the affected pools. Quick notes:
- The spike correlates with the 2026-08-14 05:58 UTC model version roll (v5.1.2) and a kernel optimization push on that same fleet. The majority of latency increase appears in attention kernel hot paths for longer-sequence buckets.

Technical mitigation (detailed):
1) Canary revert: deploy v5.1.0 to a 20% subset of east-us-2 (selector: pool-id eu2a-worker-*) at 10:45 UTC. Monitor p95, p50, and 5xxs.
2) Monitoring triggers: automatic abort if p95 > 300ms after 30m or 5xx > 0.5% absolute increase.
3) Fallback plan: if revert doesn't hit targets, we will route traffic to quantized 5c-q8 variant for the affected region for up to 72 hours while we hotfix compilation kernels / attention optimizations.
4) Communication plan: Customer-facing status updates at T+30m and T+2h; internal postmortem link to follow.

SLA waiver: I support a narrowly scoped waiver tied to model-5c:v5.1.2 for 48 hours for Acme Robotics only, conditioned on our mitigation steps above and daily executive summaries. We'll also record a temporary SLO adjustment in the account record.

Operational ask for approvals:
- Rishi: pricing/credits approval in case we offer a one-time SLA credit for the incident.
- Laura: permission to notify customer and request formal waiver.

I'll be on the runbook channel and can execute the canary as soon as we have approvals.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Danielle Harper <d.harper@acme.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spike on model-5c (v5.1.2) — acceptance of temporary SLA waiver and staged revert

Hi Laura / Marcus / team,

Thanks for the prompt analysis and the clear mitigation plan. Acme Robotics accepts the proposed narrowly scoped SLA waiver for 48 hours tied specifically to model-5c:v5.1.2 while you run the canary revert. We ask that:
- The canary be scheduled no earlier than 2026-08-14 10:45 UTC (you indicated that timing) and that we receive the T+30m status update.
- Any full revert or routing to quantized fallback must be accompanied by a short note to our ops channel and a plan for request routing to avoid demo impact.

We agree to the monitoring triggers and will hold off on escalation to legal while you proceed. Please share the Drive link and the HubSpot note once the waiver is recorded.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Danielle Harper
Director of AI Integrations
Acme Robotics
